newsitem.title: USA: Sex discrimination suit filed by Congress workers.
newsitem.headline: Sex discrimination suit filed by Congress workers.

text.p: A group of cleaning women who work at the U.S. Capitol filed a sex discrimination suit Thursday against Congress, charging that they are paid less then men who do the same jobs.
The 15 women were among 300 custodial workers, 98 percent of them women, who work for the Architect of the Capitol's office which is responsible for maintenance at the Capitol.
The women said in a statement that their duties and work have increased over several years without a comparable increase in their pay.

"We have been expected to do more -- in many cases, we are performing the same duties of jobs predominantly held by men -- without the pay men receive. It's about time that the Architect of the Capitol recognised the concept of equal pay for equal work," Dolores Jones, one of the workers, said.
The women will be represented in the suit by the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees.

Last year, Congress passed a law to make congressional employees subject to the same laws against job discrimination as all other workers and to give them the right to organise and join labour unions. Until then, they had no job protection and could be fired at will.
